content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (fallback target).**

- **Customer Data (already met):** § 17.1 makes us "the sole and exclusive owner of all Customer Data and other Confidential Information", and § 17.4 confines M&I's use of that information to "the purposes contemplated by this Agreement" — no broad Vendor licence to distribute or exploit our data exists, so no edit was needed there.
- **Failure point:** § 10.4 vests in M&I every writing or work of authorship created in performing the Services "even if paid for by Customer" (Developed Software), with resale to other M&I customers and only a partial refund/credit, while § 17.2 limits us to use "during the Term". We hold no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify or sublicense custom work we fund — a fallback failure.
- **Cure (shortest at fallback):** a new § 10.5 granting us a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software for our business, plus a six-word conforming carve-out in § 17.2 so the Term-only limitation no longer contradicts the new licence. M&I's ownership of its programs, ideas and know-how, its resale right and the refund/credit mechanic are left verbatim, so no collateral rewrite is required.
